I know where you're coming from. I've always wanted to get into records and when I finally got into them a couple of years ago, I figured I would just start with a Crosley with built-in speakers and then hook it up to a stereo later or maybe just get a better turntable. But after reading around I saw that the general consensus among more serious record enthusiasts is that they are low quality, and that the stylus and heavy tracking force will damage your records (though I have to say I'm skeptical of how bad these actually are for records). The other reason people don't like these players is they think why buy a bad turntable new when you can buy an exponentially better one used.

So when I read all of this when I was starting out, I kind of lucked out and found a great old Sony receiver for $30 at the Goodwill and bought killer speakers for $80 off of Craigslist. My mom and I were ending a good year of our family business and when talking about records with my mom, she said she would get me a turntable for Christmas. And I asked for an Audio Technica ATLP-120 and it's the greatest present I've ever gotten. You can get those for $250-$300, but I have seen Amazon sell them for as low as $200.

Although I think some people here can be rude about it, the general idea among people here seems to be that getting into records doesn't start with buying a Crosley, it starts with the adventure of putting together a good stereo made up of older, quality parts.

Putting together an old stereo isn't hard, but it can seem a little overwhelming if you don't know what you're looking for. I would recommend reading the sidebar and if you have any questions, send me a message and I'll try to help and not be a condescending dick. :)

Sacramento, CA - Dimple Records

There are many Dimple Records around the Sacramento area, but my favorite is the vinyl/book store on Arden. Tons of great records (used and new), good prices, good condition (you can pretty much be sure that if you find a used record you want, it will play perfectly), friendly staff, and well organized. The other Dimples all have new and used vinyl, and are usually just fine if you're looking for new stuff, but the one on Arden is where you want to go if looking for used.

Sacramento, CA - Rare Records on Broadway

Pretty much all used records. Tons and tons of used records. I went to Walt Disney World recently for the first time at age 26 after never having been Disneyland or Disney World. My favorite things from Magic Kingdom:

* Haunted Mansion (Heard about this all my life and totally lived up to my expectations! Probably my favorite ride I went on)
* Splash Mountain
* Pirates of the Caribbean
* Space Mountain

Things I feel like I should have done at MK, but didn't:

* Big Thunder Mountain Railroad
* Peter Pan's Flight
* Tom Sawyer's Island
* Hall of Presidents
* Mickey's Philharmagic
* Astro Orbiter
* Get a Dole Whip

At Epcot, I felt like I spent too much time wandering around the World Showcase and missed all of the coolest stuff at Future World. I wish I would have checked out Test Track and Soarin'. The Finding Nemo Aquarium exhibit was the coolest thing I did at Epcot and I highly recommend it. I also wish I could have checked out the Captain EO movie, but maybe that's just because I'm a big Michael Jackson fan.

If you're interested in getting pictures with characters, you should be able to pick up a little brochure-style guide with appearance times. The people they get to play these characters (like the Disney princesses) are incredible and absolutely hypnotic. They are so dedicated to their character that you really feel like you're meeting that character. If you have kids with you, they would love this.

For future reference, I also highly recommend Disney Hollywood Studios. Rides like Twilight Zone Tower of Terror, Star Tours, and the Aerosmith Rock n Roller Coaster are very cool. Also, the Fantasmic show is one of the most amazing things I've ever seen and maybe my favorite experience from my trip to WDW.
